key_insight: Microstructure-dependent recurrent neural operators can approximate homogenized Kelvin–Voigt constitutive laws in 2D and 3D, with a sufficient internal-variable dimension growing logarithmically in inverse relative stress error and material contrast.
engineering_relevance: These surrogates aim to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations while capturing loading-history dependence across heterogeneous microstructures.
method: Use internal variables to build a Markovian approximation of material memory.
Represent microstructure-dependent constitutive responses with neural operators.
Use the memory kernel’s spectral representation to prove uniform approximation and bound internal-variable dimension.
evidence_signal: Viscoelasticity and crystal-plasticity experiments examine internal-variable dimension and sample complexity, while the theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.
watch_item: The approximation guarantees concern periodic Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity; crystal plasticity is supported by numerical experiments rather than the stated theory.
paper_title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
